 # Sharing
 
+## Access details
+
+**2026-11-01 · SPN-071 · accepted agent decision.** Account file menus offer
+**Access details…** using the existing read-only modal, heading, secondary text,
+status and retry patterns. The primary text describes effective access:
+**Editor through Budgets**, **Viewer**, **File admin**, or **Owner**. A direct
+grant says **Shared directly with you.** No new sharing controls appear here.
+
+Only a currently readable granting ancestor may be named. The strongest grant
+wins; direct access wins an equal-strength tie, followed by the nearest matching
+ancestor. A Space page also identifies the Space boundary and explains that its
+access applies to every page and folder. Current authorization is fetched when
+the dialog opens and rechecked while visible. Loading, offline and failed states
+clear the old source rather than leaving stale private names visible. Closing
+returns focus to the originating row or document menu. Guest routes have no
+account access-details action.
+
+Production stories live in `Sharing/Access details` and the Space document-actions
+story. They cover direct/inherited/owner/File admin/Space access, long names,
+loading, failure and stale-response handling. See the rationale and persona
+effects in [SPN-071](../implementation/SPN-071.md#privacy-safe-access-provenance).
+

+# SPN-071 — Personal hiding, access provenance and live upgrades
+
+## Scope and capability checkpoint
+
+**2026-11-01 · Accepted implementation direction · agent judgment.** The complete L-sized outcome retains all three scenarios from SPN-071: personal Hide/Show hidden discovery, privacy-safe granting-ancestor details including the Space boundary, and an open viewer becoming editable without reload or lost position. Declining shares, notifications and personal pinning remain out of scope.
+
+Current-main investigation found two unconditional role-mismatch fences: the sync transport closes upgraded sockets and the client treats upgraded metadata as terminal denial. Native permissions already project Spinel grants at the public cache boundary. The implementation will reuse those boundaries, admitting only verified account-role increases on the same native unit. Downgrades, revocation, guest epochs, document generations, maintenance and account changes retain their existing fences. A real Doc and Sheet upgrade is the first capability check; no test pass is claimed in this checkpoint.
+
+Hiding remains a separate per-account discovery preference. It does not change grants, canonical parent, ownership, personal filing or prepared offline bytes. A Space is hidden as its outer file. Access details use current account authorization and expose only readable granting sources; Space children retain the outer Space sharing boundary.
+
+### Persona tradeoffs
+
+- **Collaborator:** fewer stale shares, an explanation of effective access, and live editing without losing their current work or place.
+- **Owner:** ownership, sharing and canonical organization remain authoritative; personal hiding cannot remove a document or alter a grant.
+- **Link guest:** no account discovery or provenance metadata; existing link revocation and privacy epochs remain authoritative.
+- **Operator:** no new service or background polling system; existing bounded collaboration scans and SQLite storage are reused.
+
+## Validation plan
+
+Use focused workspace/HTTP tests for personal isolation, search filtering and nonleaking provenance; native permission and transport tests for upgrade plus downgrade/revocation; production browser journeys for hide/restore and actual Doc/Sheet typing in the unchanged native unit. Cover prepared downloads and the phone document-layout restriction. Add changed production Storybook states and inspect light, dark and phone screenshots.
+
+The final PR must retain the seven required CI gates, two independent nonimplementing reviews of the same current commit, visual approval marked **agent review only**, exact source/check/review identities, measurements, and dispositions. This checkpoint is an implementation plan, not completed acceptance evidence. The original kickoff requested a mergeable PR; the later authorized backlog run resumes it through landing after all gates pass, as recorded below.
+
+## Personal hiding without changing access
+
+**2026-11-01 · Accepted · agent judgment.** The question was whether hiding should
+reuse personal filing, remove a grant or add an independent discovery preference.
+The original ticket and [personal organization decision](SPN-021.md#legacy-decision-30-trash-batches-and-exact-set-deletion)
+require the latter. A private `workspace_hidden` table records only account/item
+pairs. Authorization is checked before each change. Owners, Operators, guests,
+revoked accounts and Space children cannot use that endpoint to create unrelated
+preferences. Cascading foreign keys remove preferences with their account or item.
+
+Ordinary shared/search responses filter hidden rows. The account catalog can
+request the complete authorized inventory, carrying only a `hidden` flag, so
+**Show hidden** and cold offline launch remain useful. Search retains the complete
+graph for scope traversal and filters hidden result rows afterward. This hides
+the selected outer file, not every descendant: hidden folders remain traversable
+where the person has current access. Filed references and downloaded bundles are
+not removed. An outer Space is one preference, without independent child hiding,
+filing or grants. Existing sign-out and revocation cleanup stays authoritative.
+
+The UI composes existing menus, badges, status text and focus restoration. It
+exposes **Hide**, **Show**, and the Shared with me title menu's **Show hidden** /
+**Hide hidden**. Failed requests leave confirmed state visible; pending operations
+use the existing serialized shared-item mutation path. Personal pinning remains
+removed under [decision #128](SPN-047.md#legacy-decision-128-remove-personal-pinning).
+
+**Personas:** the Collaborator controls discovery without losing access or
+downloaded work; the Owner's grants and canonical organization are unchanged;
+the Link guest receives no account catalog; the Operator maintains one small
+SQLite preference table, with restore and sync-transition inventory updated.
+
+## Privacy-safe access provenance
+
+**2026-11-01 · Accepted · agent judgment.** Reusing cached parent labels could
+reveal an ancestor after access changed. Instead, a dedicated account-only access
+endpoint resolves the current effective role and its source in one transaction.
+It chooses the nearest readable grant matching the effective role; direct access
+wins an equal-strength tie. Stronger inherited access still wins over a weaker
+direct grant, following [first integration grooming](grooming-2026-10-17.md#legacy-decision-23-first-integration-grooming).
+Every candidate ancestor must independently be readable before its name is sent.
+Explicit Space scope cannot fall back to ordinary routes, and child grants cannot
+escape the outer Space sharing boundary from
+[decision #116](SPN-078.md#legacy-decision-116-spaces-remain-files-in-folders).
+
+The existing read-only modal presents **Editor through Budgets** or direct/owner
+access, plus the Space boundary when applicable. It fetches only while open,
+rechecks on focus/visibility/online and every five seconds, and clears old names
+on offline/hidden/error states. Request generations reject stale responses. It
+offers no grant editing and never includes other accounts' grants.
+
+**Personas:** the Collaborator learns why they can edit; the Owner retains
+private ancestor names and grant authority; the Link guest receives no account
+provenance; the Operator gets a bounded resolver and current authorization, with
+no new cached permission model. This uses existing modal/menu patterns from the
+[approved composed design](SPN-047.md#legacy-decision-126-approved-redesign-and-its-limits).
+
+## Live upgrades with current authority
+
+**2026-11-01 · Accepted · agent judgment.** The capability checkpoint established
+that public native root permission points can be changed without rebuilding a
+Doc or Sheet. The transport now accepts only monotonic account-role increases
+through its existing access scan; precommit authorization still checks every
+edit. Guests, downgrades, revocations, account changes, route mismatches, maintenance
+and replaced generations keep their existing fences. Old-role one-use tickets
+remain invalid. No new polling mechanism or SDK dependency is introduced.
+
+The existing client access check admits an upgrade only on the same live unit.
+It updates root permissions and native input controls without selecting,
+scrolling, focusing, recreating the unit or reconnecting its socket. Range,
+worksheet and paragraph policies remain in force. The generic image renderer has
+a separate edit flag from the Sheet drawing service. Independent review found
+that setting it true at upgrade could attach late image controls on a protected
+worksheet. Its flag now follows the real composite workbook/active-worksheet
+policy, including point registration, sheet changes and disposal; the SDK retains
+control of existing object transformers. Live phone Docs keep
+their reversible UI containers: Modern layout can enable editing, while
+Traditional layout and changed-layout restrictions remain read-only. Static
+snapshot behavior is unchanged.
+
+A prepared viewer first acquires the existing exclusive writer under offline
+editor admission. The durable update compares account, Space scope, generation,
+base snapshot, revision offset, SDK/schema and maintenance identity, refusing
+pending/recovery/uncertain state or a newer stored checkpoint. Only the role and
+read-only metadata change; native base/image bytes remain intact. The current
+checkpoint is then persisted before native input is enabled. Partial promotion
+is idempotent, failures remain visible and can retry, and a viewer projection
+caused by a lost writer or save failure cannot be thawed as a grant upgrade.
+
+**Personas:** the Collaborator continues at their current place and retains local
+work; the Owner's current authority still decides every durable edit; Link guest
+privacy epochs and guest role changes remain terminal; the Operator reuses the
+existing transport, scan, public permission API, storage lock and recovery fences.
+
+## Scope reassessment and verification checkpoint
+
+**2026-11-01 · Full original acceptance retained · agent judgment.** Native phone
+UI construction, drawing permissions and prepared-copy writer admission required
+investigation within the original L-sized integration outcome. No scenario is
+deferred and no follow-up substitutes for the positive role-upgrade acceptance.
+Production stories use the shipped Dashboard, AccessDetails and Space components;
+this ticket owns no remaining Redesign example.
+
+The initial local focused run passed 61 tests across eight workspace/HTTP/native
+permission/transport files (31.79 s, 956 MiB process-tree peak). Client permission,
+live-sync and offline lifecycle suites then passed all 144 tests (4.19 s). An
+earlier asynchronous writer-release assertion was corrected to await release;
+the isolated offline lifecycle rerun passed all 53 tests. Storybook type errors
+in testing-library matchers were repaired before publication. Typecheck then
+passed with a 1,829 MiB process-tree peak. The first hosted source run's Lint job
+passed after six formatting repairs. The client run's zero-valued memory sample
+is not used as a resource measurement.
+
+The default sandbox refused localhost binding; subsequent HTTP validation used
+approved escalation. Both pinned Chromium and headless-shell downloads returned
+HTML unavailable pages in this environment. Google's official mirror supplied
+the exact pinned Chrome 156.0.8078.4 headless shell; dependencies were unchanged.
+Failed downloads are not browser evidence.
+Full required CI and real browser/screenshot results, exact source and check
+identities, independent findings/dispositions and visual approval belong in
+[PR #226](https://github.com/mxbaylee/spinel/pull/226) before it becomes ready.
+
+## Local production acceptance
+
+**2026-11-01 · Observed passes · agent verification.** The pinned production build
+completed in 3.73 s with a 1,589 MiB process-tree peak. Actual browser runs then
+verified the complete original acceptance:
+
+| Run | Result | Time / process-tree peak |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| Desktop Doc/Sheet upgrade plus hide/show/search | 3 passed; unchanged native canvas, focus and selection, first input persisted, then downgrade/revocation refused edits | 17.6 s / 1,560 MiB, including the preceding drawing-policy test process |
+| Prepared viewer Doc/Sheet and Modern/Traditional phone Docs | 4 passed; exclusive offline writer, new offline edits replayed once, Modern touch editing enabled, Traditional phone fence preserved | 31.0 s / 1,855 MiB |
+| Hidden prepared copy, cold offline discovery, revoke, sign-out and explicit deletion | 1 passed; exact bundle retained while hidden, clean revocation cleanup, account exit locks access, explicit deletion removes bytes, remote logout completes | 16.2 s; subsequent typecheck also passed / combined peak 1,809 MiB |
+| Generic Sheet drawing policy boundary | 2 passed using real native workbook, permission and drawing services, including a simulated late renderer flag read | 7.90 s, before the desktop browser run |
+
+The desktop fixture measured grant-to-editable at 98 ms for Doc and 325 ms for
+Sheet, with navigation count unchanged at one in both. These are individual local
+observations, not a performance guarantee. The native position and saved content
+assertions establish continuation rather than merely a changed status label.
+
+The first cleanup test incorrectly expected sign-out to delete a clean copy.
+Current account-exit policy keeps clean copies locked until explicit deletion.
+The corrected fixture verifies that lock and exact retention, then confirms the
+separate deletion and server logout; no production cleanup behavior was changed.
+
+The local development browser workload and standard Storybook build exceeded the
+2 GiB cap (2,177 and 2,195 MiB observed respectively) and were stopped by the
+watchdog. They are not passes. Production acceptance stayed within the cap;
+hosted CI retains both development and production coverage. Current source/check
+identities, full CI, screenshots and independent review dispositions are recorded
+in the PR before readiness.
+
+## Visual evidence
+
+The supported Storybook `--test` build enabled local review within the cap while
+retaining shipped components and play functions; the standard hosted build is
+unchanged. All 85 changed story/theme/viewport combinations passed in 56.318 s,
+with a combined build/capture peak of 1,935 MiB. The first run exposed an assertion
+mismatch: Base UI menu items use `aria-disabled`, which Testing Library's native
+`toBeDisabled` matcher does not recognize. The story now asserts the actual ARIA
+contract. Production code did not change to satisfy that test.
+
+Eleven useful, unmodified light/dark/phone images, exact source identity, runtime
+and font provenance, all checked state IDs and file hashes are retained in
+[the evidence folder](evidence/SPN-071/README.md). Independent visual findings and
+approval are recorded in the PR against the final reviewed commit as
+**agent review only**; the automated pass alone is not approval.
+
+## Resumption on current main
+
+**2026-11-01 · Validation pending · authorized backlog run.** The prior worker
+finished its turn with draft PR #226 at `31d9e6a9ca6594153ce08710910409752c95d3fe`;
+its full CI was cancelled before completion and no final numerical grades were
+recorded. The owner subsequently requested completion of the entire pre-launch
+backlog. Recent branch activity and the prior chat were checked before resuming.
+SPN-090 remains actively owned; SPN-071 is the next eligible ticket.
+
+Current main `df1d910822cba284178f26ac4f6cf359ddcfacef` includes SPN-124 and SPN-065.
+Integration keeps all original hiding, provenance and live-upgrade acceptance,
+the new native/dashboard copy flows, retained uncertain copy outcomes and the
+connection-publication guard. Merge conflicts concern ticket retirement and
+generated backlog bookkeeping; retain main's allocated IDs/completions, append
+SPN-071 and regenerate the index. No new ticket ID, scope split or deferred
+acceptance is introduced. Existing persona decisions remain applicable.
+
+The resumed Verify plan follows the current sustainable-testing policy:
+
+- Workspace hiding/access HTTP and resolver tests own per-account discovery,
+  search and nonleaking ancestor/Space provenance. Transport and native/client

+- Existing `e2e/access-upgrade.spec.ts` and `e2e/hidden-shares.spec.ts` own actual

+- Existing copy journeys check the integrated native/dashboard copy behavior;

+- Preserve existing CI routing for workspace/access, collaboration, native editor,

+

+
+## Resumed integration findings and repair
+
+**2026-11-01 · Observed local passes · agent review only.** Two independent
+nonimplementing reviewers found the integrated phone upgrade restored Edit but
+left the native Done menu hidden, and that the surrounding Dashboard retained
+the initial viewer role. Negative controls reproduced both defects. Restore
+`HEADER_MENU` only for an allowed mobile upgrade; publish the verified role to
+the existing current-item metadata without fetching/remounting the editor.
+The Traditional phone layout fence remains effective even when its account gains
+editing. Both reviewers independently found the callback lifetime/current-item
+guard sound; final exact-commit grades and visual approval remain required.
+
+The Owner gains accurate sharing/admin actions; the Collaborator keeps current
+selection, focus and truthful access feedback; the Operator retains the existing
+account/unit/generation and offline writer checks; Link guests receive no new
+authority or provenance path. This repairs the accepted outcome without adding
+an optimistic grant, new permission cache or parallel synchronization mechanism.
+
+The existing desktop regression now checks Doc/editor and Sheet/admin headers,
+admin Rename availability and original native position/save/denial assertions.
+Phone coverage exercises real touch entry and Done exit. Its two ordinary cases

+owners remain, duplicate instrumented runs are omitted only in routine mode,

+six-versus-ten case collections agree. No environment, retry or timeout gate was
+weakened. The newly merged phone-copy fixture now expects the intentional live
+upgrade viewer message, preserving its complete retained-outcome assertions.
+
+Historical source `f653e24f34e9e7af3d6eb3bdc794fa4178b5bbe8`, under the local
+dependency state qualified below, passed seven ordinary production
+upgrade/hide/copy journeys, one hidden offline lifecycle journey, two prepared

+

+

+## Integration after SPN-132 and evidence qualification
+
+**2026-11-02 · Acceptance pending · authorized backlog run.** Fresh branch and
+ownership checks found SPN-090 idle but still blocked at its documented Chrome
+execution and Firefox native-control prerequisites. Its full outcome remains
+open in PR #224. Resume SPN-071 after its independently useful prerequisite,
+[SPN-132 PR #233](https://github.com/mxbaylee/spinel/pull/233), landed as
+`cc8364693791d981b86e80efc40bedba7fff2c08`. Integrate that current main without

+role-upgrade acceptance. Conflicts are only ticket retirement and generated
+backlog bookkeeping: retain main's IDs/completions, append SPN-071, and regenerate

+
+### Preserve the failed native timing result
+
+Source `53ad6848d79b7b5034db6f6e99a107a518f5d9e5` passed all selected code jobs
+except mobile responsiveness in CI `41403554716`; the aggregate failed correctly.
+The third unprofiled attempt-0 sample observed a 165.8 ms capacity flush against
+the unchanged 100 ms limit. Exact content, selection/history and peer/save checks
+were retained, but the failed budget prevented acceptance. [Original raw failure](https://github.com/mxbaylee/spinel/tree/077692be14832b230ce5ec705b4f8557d1b08597/docs/review-assets/spn-071-mobile-first-failure)
+and the [bounded diagnostic](https://github.com/mxbaylee/spinel/tree/593a65d9a3aadfca48c4a7c875077a3c950186e1/docs/review-assets/spn-071-flush-diagnostic)
+remain immutable. The diagnostic also failed at 113.5 ms unprofiled and 197.7 ms
+profiled. Its retained CPU profile and partial trace attribute most of that
+instrumented peak to GC; they do not establish either untraced failure's cause.
+No forced GC, subtraction, timing-limit change or assertion retry supplies a pass.
+
+The finite native-cache investigation exposed a pre-existing eligibility mismatch:
+sync capture supplies an own `__textXPreserveParagraphIds: true` marker, which the
+existing balanced-composition guard rejected. SPN-132 separately corrected only

+# Resumed integration evidence
+
+Application and test source: `f653e24f34e9e7af3d6eb3bdc794fa4178b5bbe8`, on
+main `df1d910822cba284178f26ac4f6cf359ddcfacef`. Validation ran on the identical
+uncommitted tree immediately before that commit. The evidence commit changes
+only documentation and retained artifacts. [manifest.json](manifest.json)
+records source/artifact SHA-256 hashes, runtime, cases, elapsed time and observed
+process-tree memory peaks. All workloads used the repository serial lock and
+the 2 GiB memory-pressure watchdog; all acceptance browser cases used zero retries.
+
+Fourteen unmodified PNGs show the actual integrated production app in light and
+dark themes. `shared-menu-desktop` and `access-details-desktop` use 1280×900;
+`hidden-shares-phone` and all native `phone-*` states use 390×844 Chromium
+emulation. They are not physical-device evidence. The menu includes Make a copy,
+Access details and Hide. The Modern viewer gains native Edit/Done and a current
+Can edit header without replacing its canvas; Traditional keeps its phone layout
+restriction while reporting the new account role. Earlier component proposals
+remain in the parent folder; final current component review and exact-commit
+hosted checks are linked in PR #226. **Agent review only.**
+
+## First failures and controls
+
+- `negative-authoring`: the first new phone assertion incorrectly expected Edit
+  alone to focus the native input. The existing real touch helper supplies the
+  required canvas tap; this was a test-authoring correction, not a product fix.
+- `negative-done`: the corrected regression on `7c137138580ebac6fbed947276e2fd9b9538c99f`
+  fails because native Done is absent. Restoring `HEADER_MENU` on an allowed
+  upgrade repairs it. The two phone cases then passed (10.095 s / 1,365.1 MiB).
+- `negative-header`: on that same application plus the single `HEADER_MENU`
+  repair, the desktop Doc becomes editable but still reports View only. The
+  saved regression fails expecting Can edit (9.923 s / 1,326.1 MiB). Verified
+  role propagation to existing Dashboard metadata fixes the mismatch without
+  taking its loading/remount path. The final seven-case run also checks a Sheet
+  admin's header/Rename action, same native canvas/focus/selection, actual saved
+  edits, and subsequent downgrade/revocation rejection.
+- `copy-stale-status`: the first combined integration run passed four cases and
+  failed the phone-copy fixture's old “reload after your access changes” text
+  (44.714 s / 1,472.3 MiB). SPN-071 intentionally supports live upgrades; updating
+  that assertion to View only preserves the complete retained-copy journey,
+  which passes in the final seven-case run. No copy behavior was weakened.
+- One preliminary header command collected zero tests because an anchored grep
+  ignored Playwright's project/file prefix (1.681 s / 662.8 MiB). The corrected
+  grep produced the retained negative control above; zero tests is not a pass.
+
+Raw failure screenshots, accessibility contexts and available diagnostics are
+retained here. Regression source snapshots use `.ts.txt` to keep historical
+fixtures out of compilation. Earlier resource aborts remain disclosed in the
+implementation record; none is counted as acceptance.
+
+The routing collections prove each Modern/Traditional upgrade case remains in
+development, production and mobile HTTPS during routine CI, while full
+compatibility retains both additional sync projects. These cases assert native
+UI/authority, not protocol instrumentation; prepared upgrade cases continue to
+own instrumented offline admission and replay. All nine plan tests passed.

+async function composeText(page: Page, phase: 'start' | 'update' | 'end', text: string) {
+  await input(page).evaluate(
+    (node, { phase, text }) => {
+      if (phase === 'start') {
+        node.dispatchEvent(new CompositionEvent('compositionstart', { bubbles: true, data: '' }));
+        return;
+      }
+      // Exercise the mounted native input controller through public DOM events,
+      // including the browser-owned input text. This is not a physical OS IME run.
+      node.textContent = text;
+      const selection = window.getSelection();
+      selection?.selectAllChildren(node);
+      selection?.collapseToEnd();
+      node.dispatchEvent(
+        new CompositionEvent(phase === 'update' ? 'compositionupdate' : 'compositionend', {
+          bubbles: true,
+          data: text,
+        }),
+      );
+      if (phase === 'update')
+        node.dispatchEvent(
+          new InputEvent('input', {
+            bubbles: true,
+            inputType: 'insertCompositionText',
+            data: text,
+            isComposing: true,

+        );
+    },
+    { phase, text },

+    await touch.send('Input.dispatchTouchEvent', { type: 'touchEnd', touchPoints: [] });

+async function keyboardOcclusion(page: Page, height: number) {
+  await page.evaluate((height) => {

+# SPN-071 — Personal hiding, access provenance and live upgrades
+
+## Scope and capability checkpoint
+
+**2026-11-01 · Accepted implementation direction · agent judgment.** The complete L-sized outcome retains all three scenarios from SPN-071: personal Hide/Show hidden discovery, privacy-safe granting-ancestor details including the Space boundary, and an open viewer becoming editable without reload or lost position. Declining shares, notifications and personal pinning remain out of scope.
+
+Current-main investigation found two unconditional role-mismatch fences: the sync transport closes upgraded sockets and the client treats upgraded metadata as terminal denial. Native permissions already project Spinel grants at the public cache boundary. The implementation will reuse those boundaries, admitting only verified account-role increases on the same native unit. Downgrades, revocation, guest epochs, document generations, maintenance and account changes retain their existing fences. A real Doc and Sheet upgrade is the first capability check; no test pass is claimed in this checkpoint.
+
+Hiding remains a separate per-account discovery preference. It does not change grants, canonical parent, ownership, personal filing or prepared offline bytes. A Space is hidden as its outer file. Access details use current account authorization and expose only readable granting sources; Space children retain the outer Space sharing boundary.
+
+### Persona tradeoffs
+
+- **Collaborator:** fewer stale shares, an explanation of effective access, and live editing without losing their current work or place.
+- **Owner:** ownership, sharing and canonical organization remain authoritative; personal hiding cannot remove a document or alter a grant.
+- **Link guest:** no account discovery or provenance metadata; existing link revocation and privacy epochs remain authoritative.
+- **Operator:** no new service or background polling system; existing bounded collaboration scans and SQLite storage are reused.
+

+## Personal hiding without changing access
+
+**2026-11-01 · Accepted · agent judgment.** The question was whether hiding should
+reuse personal filing, remove a grant or add an independent discovery preference.
+The original ticket and [personal organization decision](SPN-021.md#legacy-decision-30-trash-batches-and-exact-set-deletion)
+require the latter. A private `workspace_hidden` table records only account/item
+pairs. Authorization is checked before each change. Owners, Operators, guests,
+revoked accounts and Space children cannot use that endpoint to create unrelated
+preferences. Cascading foreign keys remove preferences with their account or item.
+
+Ordinary shared/search responses filter hidden rows. The account catalog can
+request the complete authorized inventory, carrying only a `hidden` flag, so
+**Show hidden** and cold offline launch remain useful. Search retains the complete
+graph for scope traversal and filters hidden result rows afterward. This hides
+the selected outer file, not every descendant: hidden folders remain traversable
+where the person has current access. Filed references and downloaded bundles are
+not removed. An outer Space is one preference, without independent child hiding,
+filing or grants. Existing sign-out and revocation cleanup stays authoritative.
+
+The UI composes existing menus, badges, status text and focus restoration. It
+exposes **Hide**, **Show**, and the Shared with me title menu's **Show hidden** /
+**Hide hidden**. Failed requests leave confirmed state visible; pending operations
+use the existing serialized shared-item mutation path. Personal pinning remains
+removed under [decision #128](SPN-047.md#legacy-decision-128-remove-personal-pinning).
+
+**Personas:** the Collaborator controls discovery without losing access or
+downloaded work; the Owner's grants and canonical organization are unchanged;
+the Link guest receives no account catalog; the Operator maintains one small
+SQLite preference table, with restore and sync-transition inventory updated.
+
+## Privacy-safe access provenance
+
+**2026-11-01 · Accepted · agent judgment.** Reusing cached parent labels could
+reveal an ancestor after access changed. Instead, a dedicated account-only access
+endpoint resolves the current effective role and its source in one transaction.
+It chooses the nearest readable grant matching the effective role; direct access
+wins an equal-strength tie. Stronger inherited access still wins over a weaker
+direct grant, following [first integration grooming](grooming-2026-10-17.md#legacy-decision-23-first-integration-grooming).
+Every candidate ancestor must independently be readable before its name is sent.
+Explicit Space scope cannot fall back to ordinary routes, and child grants cannot
+escape the outer Space sharing boundary from
+[decision #116](SPN-078.md#legacy-decision-116-spaces-remain-files-in-folders).
+
+The existing read-only modal presents **Editor through Budgets** or direct/owner
+access, plus the Space boundary when applicable. It fetches only while open,
+rechecks on focus/visibility/online and every five seconds, and clears old names
+on offline/hidden/error states. Request generations reject stale responses. It
+offers no grant editing and never includes other accounts' grants.
+
+**Personas:** the Collaborator learns why they can edit; the Owner retains
+private ancestor names and grant authority; the Link guest receives no account
+provenance; the Operator gets a bounded resolver and current authorization, with
+no new cached permission model. This uses existing modal/menu patterns from the
+[approved composed design](SPN-047.md#legacy-decision-126-approved-redesign-and-its-limits).

+# Resumed integration evidence
+
+Application and test source: `f653e24f34e9e7af3d6eb3bdc794fa4178b5bbe8`, on
+main `df1d910822cba284178f26ac4f6cf359ddcfacef`. Validation ran on the identical
+uncommitted tree immediately before that commit. The evidence commit changes
+only documentation and retained artifacts. [manifest.json](manifest.json)
+records source/artifact SHA-256 hashes, runtime, cases, elapsed time and observed
+process-tree memory peaks. All workloads used the repository serial lock and
+the 2 GiB memory-pressure watchdog; all acceptance browser cases used zero retries.
+
+Fourteen unmodified PNGs show the actual integrated production app in light and
+dark themes. `shared-menu-desktop` and `access-details-desktop` use 1280×900;
+`hidden-shares-phone` and all native `phone-*` states use 390×844 Chromium
+emulation. They are not physical-device evidence. The menu includes Make a copy,
+Access details and Hide. The Modern viewer gains native Edit/Done and a current
+Can edit header without replacing its canvas; Traditional keeps its phone layout
+restriction while reporting the new account role. Earlier component proposals
+remain in the parent folder; final current component review and exact-commit
+hosted checks are linked in PR #226. **Agent review only.**
+
+## First failures and controls
+
+- `negative-authoring`: the first new phone assertion incorrectly expected Edit
+  alone to focus the native input. The existing real touch helper supplies the
+  required canvas tap; this was a test-authoring correction, not a product fix.
+- `negative-done`: the corrected regression on `7c137138580ebac6fbed947276e2fd9b9538c99f`
+  fails because native Done is absent. Restoring `HEADER_MENU` on an allowed
+  upgrade repairs it. The two phone cases then passed (10.095 s / 1,365.1 MiB).
+- `negative-header`: on that same application plus the single `HEADER_MENU`
+  repair, the desktop Doc becomes editable but still reports View only. The
+  saved regression fails expecting Can edit (9.923 s / 1,326.1 MiB). Verified
+  role propagation to existing Dashboard metadata fixes the mismatch without
+  taking its loading/remount path. The final seven-case run also checks a Sheet
+  admin's header/Rename action, same native canvas/focus/selection, actual saved
+  edits, and subsequent downgrade/revocation rejection.
+- `copy-stale-status`: the first combined integration run passed four cases and
+  failed the phone-copy fixture's old “reload after your access changes” text
+  (44.714 s / 1,472.3 MiB). SPN-071 intentionally supports live upgrades; updating
+  that assertion to View only preserves the complete retained-copy journey,
+  which passes in the final seven-case run. No copy behavior was weakened.
+- One preliminary header command collected zero tests because an anchored grep
+  ignored Playwright's project/file prefix (1.681 s / 662.8 MiB). The corrected
+  grep produced the retained negative control above; zero tests is not a pass.
+
+Raw failure screenshots, accessibility contexts and available diagnostics are
+retained here. Regression source snapshots use `.ts.txt` to keep historical
+fixtures out of compilation. Earlier resource aborts remain disclosed in the
+implementation record; none is counted as acceptance.
+
+The routing collections prove each Modern/Traditional upgrade case remains in
+development, production and mobile HTTPS during routine CI, while full
+compatibility retains both additional sync projects. These cases assert native
+UI/authority, not protocol instrumentation; prepared upgrade cases continue to
+own instrumented offline admission and replay. All nine plan tests passed.

+      node.textContent = text;

+      selection?.selectAllChildren(node);
+      selection?.collapseToEnd();
+      node.dispatchEvent(

+# SPN-071 — Personal hiding, access provenance and live upgrades
+
+## Scope and capability checkpoint
+
+**2026-11-01 · Accepted implementation direction · agent judgment.** The complete L-sized outcome retains all three scenarios from SPN-071: personal Hide/Show hidden discovery, privacy-safe granting-ancestor details including the Space boundary, and an open viewer becoming editable without reload or lost position. Declining shares, notifications and personal pinning remain out of scope.
+
+Current-main investigation found two unconditional role-mismatch fences: the sync transport closes upgraded sockets and the client treats upgraded metadata as terminal denial. Native permissions already project Spinel grants at the public cache boundary. The implementation will reuse those boundaries, admitting only verified account-role increases on the same native unit. Downgrades, revocation, guest epochs, document generations, maintenance and account changes retain their existing fences. A real Doc and Sheet upgrade is the first capability check; no test pass is claimed in this checkpoint.
+
+Hiding remains a separate per-account discovery preference. It does not change grants, canonical parent, ownership, personal filing or prepared offline bytes. A Space is hidden as its outer file. Access details use current account authorization and expose only readable granting sources; Space children retain the outer Space sharing boundary.
+
+### Persona tradeoffs
+
+- **Collaborator:** fewer stale shares, an explanation of effective access, and live editing without losing their current work or place.
+- **Owner:** ownership, sharing and canonical organization remain authoritative; personal hiding cannot remove a document or alter a grant.
+- **Link guest:** no account discovery or provenance metadata; existing link revocation and privacy epochs remain authoritative.
+- **Operator:** no new service or background polling system; existing bounded collaboration scans and SQLite storage are reused.
+
+## Validation plan
+
+Use focused workspace/HTTP tests for personal isolation, search filtering and nonleaking provenance; native permission and transport tests for upgrade plus downgrade/revocation; production browser journeys for hide/restore and actual Doc/Sheet typing in the unchanged native unit. Cover prepared downloads and the phone document-layout restriction. Add changed production Storybook states and inspect light, dark and phone screenshots.
+
+The final PR must retain the seven required CI gates, two independent nonimplementing reviews of the same current commit, visual approval marked **agent review only**, exact source/check/review identities, measurements, and dispositions. This checkpoint is an implementation plan, not completed acceptance evidence. The original kickoff requested a mergeable PR; the later authorized backlog run resumes it through landing after all gates pass, as recorded below.
+
+## Personal hiding without changing access
+
+**2026-11-01 · Accepted · agent judgment.** The question was whether hiding should
+reuse personal filing, remove a grant or add an independent discovery preference.
+The original ticket and [personal organization decision](SPN-021.md#legacy-decision-30-trash-batches-and-exact-set-deletion)
+require the latter. A private `workspace_hidden` table records only account/item
+pairs. Authorization is checked before each change. Owners, Operators, guests,
+revoked accounts and Space children cannot use that endpoint to create unrelated
+preferences. Cascading foreign keys remove preferences with their account or item.
+
+Ordinary shared/search responses filter hidden rows. The account catalog can
+request the complete authorized inventory, carrying only a `hidden` flag, so
+**Show hidden** and cold offline launch remain useful. Search retains the complete
+graph for scope traversal and filters hidden result rows afterward. This hides
+the selected outer file, not every descendant: hidden folders remain traversable
+where the person has current access. Filed references and downloaded bundles are
+not removed. An outer Space is one preference, without independent child hiding,
+filing or grants. Existing sign-out and revocation cleanup stays authoritative.
+
+The UI composes existing menus, badges, status text and focus restoration. It
+exposes **Hide**, **Show**, and the Shared with me title menu's **Show hidden** /
+**Hide hidden**. Failed requests leave confirmed state visible; pending operations
+use the existing serialized shared-item mutation path. Personal pinning remains
+removed under [decision #128](SPN-047.md#legacy-decision-128-remove-personal-pinning).
+
+**Personas:** the Collaborator controls discovery without losing access or
+downloaded work; the Owner's grants and canonical organization are unchanged;
+the Link guest receives no account catalog; the Operator maintains one small
+SQLite preference table, with restore and sync-transition inventory updated.
+
+## Privacy-safe access provenance
+
+**2026-11-01 · Accepted · agent judgment.** Reusing cached parent labels could
+reveal an ancestor after access changed. Instead, a dedicated account-only access
+endpoint resolves the current effective role and its source in one transaction.
+It chooses the nearest readable grant matching the effective role; direct access
+wins an equal-strength tie. Stronger inherited access still wins over a weaker
+direct grant, following [first integration grooming](grooming-2026-10-17.md#legacy-decision-23-first-integration-grooming).
+Every candidate ancestor must independently be readable before its name is sent.
+Explicit Space scope cannot fall back to ordinary routes, and child grants cannot
+escape the outer Space sharing boundary from
+[decision #116](SPN-078.md#legacy-decision-116-spaces-remain-files-in-folders).
+
+The existing read-only modal presents **Editor through Budgets** or direct/owner
+access, plus the Space boundary when applicable. It fetches only while open,
+rechecks on focus/visibility/online and every five seconds, and clears old names
+on offline/hidden/error states. Request generations reject stale responses. It
+offers no grant editing and never includes other accounts' grants.
+
+**Personas:** the Collaborator learns why they can edit; the Owner retains
+private ancestor names and grant authority; the Link guest receives no account
+provenance; the Operator gets a bounded resolver and current authorization, with
+no new cached permission model. This uses existing modal/menu patterns from the
+[approved composed design](SPN-047.md#legacy-decision-126-approved-redesign-and-its-limits).
+
+## Live upgrades with current authority
+
+**2026-11-01 · Accepted · agent judgment.** The capability checkpoint established
+that public native root permission points can be changed without rebuilding a
+Doc or Sheet. The transport now accepts only monotonic account-role increases
+through its existing access scan; precommit authorization still checks every
+edit. Guests, downgrades, revocations, account changes, route mismatches, maintenance
+and replaced generations keep their existing fences. Old-role one-use tickets
+remain invalid. No new polling mechanism or SDK dependency is introduced.
+
+The existing client access check admits an upgrade only on the same live unit.
+It updates root permissions and native input controls without selecting,
+scrolling, focusing, recreating the unit or reconnecting its socket. Range,
+worksheet and paragraph policies remain in force. The generic image renderer has
+a separate edit flag from the Sheet drawing service. Independent review found
+that setting it true at upgrade could attach late image controls on a protected
+worksheet. Its flag now follows the real composite workbook/active-worksheet
+policy, including point registration, sheet changes and disposal; the SDK retains
+control of existing object transformers. Live phone Docs keep
+their reversible UI containers: Modern layout can enable editing, while
+Traditional layout and changed-layout restrictions remain read-only. Static
+snapshot behavior is unchanged.
+
+A prepared viewer first acquires the existing exclusive writer under offline
+editor admission. The durable update compares account, Space scope, generation,
+base snapshot, revision offset, SDK/schema and maintenance identity, refusing
+pending/recovery/uncertain state or a newer stored checkpoint. Only the role and
+read-only metadata change; native base/image bytes remain intact. The current
+checkpoint is then persisted before native input is enabled. Partial promotion
+is idempotent, failures remain visible and can retry, and a viewer projection
+caused by a lost writer or save failure cannot be thawed as a grant upgrade.
+
+**Personas:** the Collaborator continues at their current place and retains local
+work; the Owner's current authority still decides every durable edit; Link guest
+privacy epochs and guest role changes remain terminal; the Operator reuses the
+existing transport, scan, public permission API, storage lock and recovery fences.
+
+## Scope reassessment and verification checkpoint
+
+**2026-11-01 · Full original acceptance retained · agent judgment.** Native phone
+UI construction, drawing permissions and prepared-copy writer admission required
+investigation within the original L-sized integration outcome. No scenario is
+deferred and no follow-up substitutes for the positive role-upgrade acceptance.
+Production stories use the shipped Dashboard, AccessDetails and Space components;
+this ticket owns no remaining Redesign example.
+
+The initial local focused run passed 61 tests across eight workspace/HTTP/native
+permission/transport files (31.79 s, 956 MiB process-tree peak). Client permission,
+live-sync and offline lifecycle suites then passed all 144 tests (4.19 s). An
+earlier asynchronous writer-release assertion was corrected to await release;
+the isolated offline lifecycle rerun passed all 53 tests. Storybook type errors
+in testing-library matchers were repaired before publication. Typecheck then
+passed with a 1,829 MiB process-tree peak. The first hosted source run's Lint job
+passed after six formatting repairs. The client run's zero-valued memory sample
+is not used as a resource measurement.
+
+The default sandbox refused localhost binding; subsequent HTTP validation used
+approved escalation. Both pinned Chromium and headless-shell downloads returned
+HTML unavailable pages in this environment. Google's official mirror supplied
+the exact pinned Chrome 156.0.8078.4 headless shell; dependencies were unchanged.
+Failed downloads are not browser evidence.
+Full required CI and real browser/screenshot results, exact source and check
+identities, independent findings/dispositions and visual approval belong in
+[PR #226](https://github.com/mxbaylee/spinel/pull/226) before it becomes ready.
+
+## Local production acceptance
+
+**2026-11-01 · Observed passes · agent verification.** The pinned production build
+completed in 3.73 s with a 1,589 MiB process-tree peak. Actual browser runs then
+verified the complete original acceptance:
+

+      node.textContent = text;

+      selection?.selectAllChildren(node);
+      selection?.collapseToEnd();
+      node.dispatchEvent(
+        new CompositionEvent(phase === 'update' ? 'compositionupdate' : 'compositionend', {
+          bubbles: true,
+          data: text,

+            inputType: 'insertCompositionText',

+# SPN-071 — Personal hiding, access provenance and live upgrades
+
+## Scope and capability checkpoint
+
+**2026-11-01 · Accepted implementation direction · agent judgment.** The complete L-sized outcome retains all three scenarios from SPN-071: personal Hide/Show hidden discovery, privacy-safe granting-ancestor details including the Space boundary, and an open viewer becoming editable without reload or lost position. Declining shares, notifications and personal pinning remain out of scope.
+
+Current-main investigation found two unconditional role-mismatch fences: the sync transport closes upgraded sockets and the client treats upgraded metadata as terminal denial. Native permissions already project Spinel grants at the public cache boundary. The implementation will reuse those boundaries, admitting only verified account-role increases on the same native unit. Downgrades, revocation, guest epochs, document generations, maintenance and account changes retain their existing fences. A real Doc and Sheet upgrade is the first capability check; no test pass is claimed in this checkpoint.
+
+Hiding remains a separate per-account discovery preference. It does not change grants, canonical parent, ownership, personal filing or prepared offline bytes. A Space is hidden as its outer file. Access details use current account authorization and expose only readable granting sources; Space children retain the outer Space sharing boundary.
+
+### Persona tradeoffs
+
+- **Collaborator:** fewer stale shares, an explanation of effective access, and live editing without losing their current work or place.
+- **Owner:** ownership, sharing and canonical organization remain authoritative; personal hiding cannot remove a document or alter a grant.
+- **Link guest:** no account discovery or provenance metadata; existing link revocation and privacy epochs remain authoritative.
+- **Operator:** no new service or background polling system; existing bounded collaboration scans and SQLite storage are reused.
+
+## Validation plan
+
+Use focused workspace/HTTP tests for personal isolation, search filtering and nonleaking provenance; native permission and transport tests for upgrade plus downgrade/revocation; production browser journeys for hide/restore and actual Doc/Sheet typing in the unchanged native unit. Cover prepared downloads and the phone document-layout restriction. Add changed production Storybook states and inspect light, dark and phone screenshots.
+
+The final PR must retain the seven required CI gates, two independent nonimplementing reviews of the same current commit, visual approval marked **agent review only**, exact source/check/review identities, measurements, and dispositions. This checkpoint is an implementation plan, not completed acceptance evidence. The original kickoff requested a mergeable PR; the later authorized backlog run resumes it through landing after all gates pass, as recorded below.
+
+## Personal hiding without changing access
+
+**2026-11-01 · Accepted · agent judgment.** The question was whether hiding should
+reuse personal filing, remove a grant or add an independent discovery preference.
+The original ticket and [personal organization decision](SPN-021.md#legacy-decision-30-trash-batches-and-exact-set-deletion)
+require the latter. A private `workspace_hidden` table records only account/item
+pairs. Authorization is checked before each change. Owners, Operators, guests,
+revoked accounts and Space children cannot use that endpoint to create unrelated
+preferences. Cascading foreign keys remove preferences with their account or item.
+
+Ordinary shared/search responses filter hidden rows. The account catalog can
+request the complete authorized inventory, carrying only a `hidden` flag, so
+**Show hidden** and cold offline launch remain useful. Search retains the complete
+graph for scope traversal and filters hidden result rows afterward. This hides
+the selected outer file, not every descendant: hidden folders remain traversable
+where the person has current access. Filed references and downloaded bundles are
+not removed. An outer Space is one preference, without independent child hiding,
+filing or grants. Existing sign-out and revocation cleanup stays authoritative.
+
+The UI composes existing menus, badges, status text and focus restoration. It
+exposes **Hide**, **Show**, and the Shared with me title menu's **Show hidden** /
+**Hide hidden**. Failed requests leave confirmed state visible; pending operations
+use the existing serialized shared-item mutation path. Personal pinning remains
+removed under [decision #128](SPN-047.md#legacy-decision-128-remove-personal-pinning).
+
+**Personas:** the Collaborator controls discovery without losing access or
+downloaded work; the Owner's grants and canonical organization are unchanged;
+the Link guest receives no account catalog; the Operator maintains one small
+SQLite preference table, with restore and sync-transition inventory updated.
+
+## Privacy-safe access provenance
+
+**2026-11-01 · Accepted · agent judgment.** Reusing cached parent labels could
+reveal an ancestor after access changed. Instead, a dedicated account-only access
+endpoint resolves the current effective role and its source in one transaction.
+It chooses the nearest readable grant matching the effective role; direct access
+wins an equal-strength tie. Stronger inherited access still wins over a weaker
+direct grant, following [first integration grooming](grooming-2026-10-17.md#legacy-decision-23-first-integration-grooming).
+Every candidate ancestor must independently be readable before its name is sent.
+Explicit Space scope cannot fall back to ordinary routes, and child grants cannot
+escape the outer Space sharing boundary from
+[decision #116](SPN-078.md#legacy-decision-116-spaces-remain-files-in-folders).
+
+The existing read-only modal presents **Editor through Budgets** or direct/owner
+access, plus the Space boundary when applicable. It fetches only while open,
+rechecks on focus/visibility/online and every five seconds, and clears old names
+on offline/hidden/error states. Request generations reject stale responses. It
+offers no grant editing and never includes other accounts' grants.
+
+**Personas:** the Collaborator learns why they can edit; the Owner retains
+private ancestor names and grant authority; the Link guest receives no account
+provenance; the Operator gets a bounded resolver and current authorization, with
+no new cached permission model. This uses existing modal/menu patterns from the
+[approved composed design](SPN-047.md#legacy-decision-126-approved-redesign-and-its-limits).
+
+## Live upgrades with current authority
+
+**2026-11-01 · Accepted · agent judgment.** The capability checkpoint established
+that public native root permission points can be changed without rebuilding a
+Doc or Sheet. The transport now accepts only monotonic account-role increases
+through its existing access scan; precommit authorization still checks every
+edit. Guests, downgrades, revocations, account changes, route mismatches, maintenance
+and replaced generations keep their existing fences. Old-role one-use tickets
+remain invalid. No new polling mechanism or SDK dependency is introduced.
+
+The existing client access check admits an upgrade only on the same live unit.
+It updates root permissions and native input controls without selecting,
+scrolling, focusing, recreating the unit or reconnecting its socket. Range,
+worksheet and paragraph policies remain in force. The generic image renderer has
+a separate edit flag from the Sheet drawing service. Independent review found
+that setting it true at upgrade could attach late image controls on a protected
+worksheet. Its flag now follows the real composite workbook/active-worksheet
+policy, including point registration, sheet changes and disposal; the SDK retains
+control of existing object transformers. Live phone Docs keep
+their reversible UI containers: Modern layout can enable editing, while
+Traditional layout and changed-layout restrictions remain read-only. Static
+snapshot behavior is unchanged.
+
+A prepared viewer first acquires the existing exclusive writer under offline
+editor admission. The durable update compares account, Space scope, generation,
+base snapshot, revision offset, SDK/schema and maintenance identity, refusing
+pending/recovery/uncertain state or a newer stored checkpoint. Only the role and
+read-only metadata change; native base/image bytes remain intact. The current
+checkpoint is then persisted before native input is enabled. Partial promotion
+is idempotent, failures remain visible and can retry, and a viewer projection
+caused by a lost writer or save failure cannot be thawed as a grant upgrade.
+
+**Personas:** the Collaborator continues at their current place and retains local
+work; the Owner's current authority still decides every durable edit; Link guest
+privacy epochs and guest role changes remain terminal; the Operator reuses the
+existing transport, scan, public permission API, storage lock and recovery fences.
+
+## Scope reassessment and verification checkpoint
+
+**2026-11-01 · Full original acceptance retained · agent judgment.** Native phone
+UI construction, drawing permissions and prepared-copy writer admission required
+investigation within the original L-sized integration outcome. No scenario is
+deferred and no follow-up substitutes for the positive role-upgrade acceptance.
+Production stories use the shipped Dashboard, AccessDetails and Space components;
+this ticket owns no remaining Redesign example.
+
+The initial local focused run passed 61 tests across eight workspace/HTTP/native
+permission/transport files (31.79 s, 956 MiB process-tree peak). Client permission,
+live-sync and offline lifecycle suites then passed all 144 tests (4.19 s). An
+earlier asynchronous writer-release assertion was corrected to await release;
+the isolated offline lifecycle rerun passed all 53 tests. Storybook type errors
+in testing-library matchers were repaired before publication. Typecheck then
+passed with a 1,829 MiB process-tree peak. The first hosted source run's Lint job
+passed after six formatting repairs. The client run's zero-valued memory sample
+is not used as a resource measurement.
+
+The default sandbox refused localhost binding; subsequent HTTP validation used
+approved escalation. Both pinned Chromium and headless-shell downloads returned
+HTML unavailable pages in this environment. Google's official mirror supplied
+the exact pinned Chrome 156.0.8078.4 headless shell; dependencies were unchanged.
+Failed downloads are not browser evidence.
+Full required CI and real browser/screenshot results, exact source and check
+identities, independent findings/dispositions and visual approval belong in
+[PR #226](https://github.com/mxbaylee/spinel/pull/226) before it becomes ready.
+
+## Local production acceptance
+
+**2026-11-01 · Observed passes · agent verification.** The pinned production build
+completed in 3.73 s with a 1,589 MiB process-tree peak. Actual browser runs then
+verified the complete original acceptance:
+
+| Run | Result | Time / process-tree peak |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| Desktop Doc/Sheet upgrade plus hide/show/search | 3 passed; unchanged native canvas, focus and selection, first input persisted, then downgrade/revocation refused edits | 17.6 s / 1,560 MiB, including the preceding drawing-policy test process |
+| Prepared viewer Doc/Sheet and Modern/Traditional phone Docs | 4 passed; exclusive offline writer, new offline edits replayed once, Modern touch editing enabled, Traditional phone fence preserved | 31.0 s / 1,855 MiB |
+| Hidden prepared copy, cold offline discovery, revoke, sign-out and explicit deletion | 1 passed; exact bundle retained while hidden, clean revocation cleanup, account exit locks access, explicit deletion removes bytes, remote logout completes | 16.2 s; subsequent typecheck also passed / combined peak 1,809 MiB |
+| Generic Sheet drawing policy boundary | 2 passed using real native workbook, permission and drawing services, including a simulated late renderer flag read | 7.90 s, before the desktop browser run |
+
+The desktop fixture measured grant-to-editable at 98 ms for Doc and 325 ms for
+Sheet, with navigation count unchanged at one in both. These are individual local
+observations, not a performance guarantee. The native position and saved content
+assertions establish continuation rather than merely a changed status label.
+
+The first cleanup test incorrectly expected sign-out to delete a clean copy.
+Current account-exit policy keeps clean copies locked until explicit deletion.
+The corrected fixture verifies that lock and exact retention, then confirms the
+separate deletion and server logout; no production cleanup behavior was changed.
+
+The local development browser workload and standard Storybook build exceeded the
+2 GiB cap (2,177 and 2,195 MiB observed respectively) and were stopped by the
+watchdog. They are not passes. Production acceptance stayed within the cap;
+hosted CI retains both development and production coverage. Current source/check
+identities, full CI, screenshots and independent review dispositions are recorded
+in the PR before readiness.
+
+## Visual evidence
+
+The supported Storybook `--test` build enabled local review within the cap while
+retaining shipped components and play functions; the standard hosted build is
+unchanged. All 85 changed story/theme/viewport combinations passed in 56.318 s,
+with a combined build/capture peak of 1,935 MiB. The first run exposed an assertion
+mismatch: Base UI menu items use `aria-disabled`, which Testing Library's native
+`toBeDisabled` matcher does not recognize. The story now asserts the actual ARIA
+contract. Production code did not change to satisfy that test.
+
+Eleven useful, unmodified light/dark/phone images, exact source identity, runtime
+and font provenance, all checked state IDs and file hashes are retained in
+[the evidence folder](evidence/SPN-071/README.md). Independent visual findings and
+approval are recorded in the PR against the final reviewed commit as
+**agent review only**; the automated pass alone is not approval.
+
+## Resumption on current main
+
+**2026-11-01 · Validation pending · authorized backlog run.** The prior worker
+finished its turn with draft PR #226 at `31d9e6a9ca6594153ce08710910409752c95d3fe`;
+its full CI was cancelled before completion and no final numerical grades were

+Integration keeps all original hiding, provenance and live-upgrade acceptance,
+the new native/dashboard copy flows, retained uncertain copy outcomes and the

+
+The resumed Verify plan follows the current sustainable-testing policy:
+
+- Workspace hiding/access HTTP and resolver tests own per-account discovery,

+## Resumed integration findings and repair

+records source/artifact SHA-256 hashes, runtime, cases, elapsed time and observed
+process-tree memory peaks. All workloads used the repository serial lock and
+the 2 GiB memory-pressure watchdog; all acceptance browser cases used zero retries.
+
+Fourteen unmodified PNGs show the actual integrated production app in light and
+dark themes. `shared-menu-desktop` and `access-details-desktop` use 1280×900;
+`hidden-shares-phone` and all native `phone-*` states use 390×844 Chromium
+emulation. They are not physical-device evidence. The menu includes Make a copy,
+Access details and Hide. The Modern viewer gains native Edit/Done and a current
+Can edit header without replacing its canvas; Traditional keeps its phone layout
+restriction while reporting the new account role. Earlier component proposals
+remain in the parent folder; final current component review and exact-commit
+hosted checks are linked in PR #226. **Agent review only.**
+
+## First failures and controls
+
+- `negative-authoring`: the first new phone assertion incorrectly expected Edit
+  alone to focus the native input. The existing real touch helper supplies the
+  required canvas tap; this was a test-authoring correction, not a product fix.
+- `negative-done`: the corrected regression on `7c137138580ebac6fbed947276e2fd9b9538c99f`
+  fails because native Done is absent. Restoring `HEADER_MENU` on an allowed
+  upgrade repairs it. The two phone cases then passed (10.095 s / 1,365.1 MiB).
+- `negative-header`: on that same application plus the single `HEADER_MENU`
+  repair, the desktop Doc becomes editable but still reports View only. The
+  saved regression fails expecting Can edit (9.923 s / 1,326.1 MiB). Verified
+  role propagation to existing Dashboard metadata fixes the mismatch without
+  taking its loading/remount path. The final seven-case run also checks a Sheet
+  admin's header/Rename action, same native canvas/focus/selection, actual saved
+  edits, and subsequent downgrade/revocation rejection.
+- `copy-stale-status`: the first combined integration run passed four cases and
+  failed the phone-copy fixture's old “reload after your access changes” text
+  (44.714 s / 1,472.3 MiB). SPN-071 intentionally supports live upgrades; updating
+  that assertion to View only preserves the complete retained-copy journey,
+  which passes in the final seven-case run. No copy behavior was weakened.
+- One preliminary header command collected zero tests because an anchored grep
+  ignored Playwright's project/file prefix (1.681 s / 662.8 MiB). The corrected
+  grep produced the retained negative control above; zero tests is not a pass.
+

+fixtures out of compilation. Earlier resource aborts remain disclosed in the
+implementation record; none is counted as acceptance.

+development, production and mobile HTTPS during routine CI, while full
+compatibility retains both additional sync projects. These cases assert native
+UI/authority, not protocol instrumentation; prepared upgrade cases continue to
+own instrumented offline admission and replay. All nine plan tests passed.

+    { phase, text },
+  );
+}
+
+interface DocSelectionEvidence {
+  unitId: string;
+  start?: number;
+  end?: number;
+  hasAnchor: boolean;
+  editing: boolean;
+  bounds?: { left: number; right: number; top: number; bottom: number };
+  scroll: number;
+  text: string;
+}
+
+async function selectFirstWord(page: Page) {
+  const point = await textPoint(page);
+  const touch = await page.context().newCDPSession(page);
+  try {
+    await touch.send('Input.dispatchTouchEvent', {
+      type: 'touchStart',
+      touchPoints: [{ x: point.centerX, y: point.y }],
+    });
+    // A genuine held touch crosses the native long-press threshold; do not
+    // substitute a programmatic text range for this selection interaction.
+    await page.waitForTimeout(650);
+    await touch.send('Input.dispatchTouchEvent', { type: 'touchEnd', touchPoints: [] });
+  } finally {
+    await touch.detach();
+  }
+}
+
+// Chromium desktop automation does not open an OS keyboard. Drive the browser
+// visual-viewport event contract explicitly; physical iOS/Android checks remain
+// separate. This exercises the native toolbar response, not an actual keyboard.
+async function keyboardOcclusion(page: Page, height: number) {
+  await page.evaluate((height) => {
+    const viewport = window.visualViewport;
+    if (!viewport) throw new Error('Visual viewport is unavailable.');
+    Reflect.deleteProperty(viewport, 'height');
+    const available = viewport.height;
+    if (height)
+      Object.defineProperty(viewport, 'height', {
+        configurable: true,
+        get: () => available - height,
+      });
+    viewport.dispatchEvent(new Event('resize'));
+  }, height);
+}
+
+async function capture(page: Page, info: TestInfo, name: string) {
+  expect(await page.evaluate(() => document.documentElement.scrollWidth <= innerWidth)).toBe(true);
+  await mkdir('test-results/theme-screenshots', { recursive: true });
+  await page.screenshot({
+    path: `test-results/theme-screenshots/spn-072-${name}-${info.project.name}.png`,
+    fullPage: true,
+    animations: 'disabled',
+  });
+}
+
+async function touchTargets(target: Locator) {
+  for (const button of await target.getByRole('button').all()) {
+    if (!(await button.isVisible())) continue;
+    const box = (await button.boundingBox())!;
+    expect(box.width).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(44);
+    expect(box.height).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(44);
+  }
+}
+
+async function fixture(

+  const paragraphs = [

+    'A readable phone paragraph wraps onto several lines without shrinking its letters. ' +
+      'Keep this whole sentence and the original saved page geometry when the screen rotates.',

+      ['scalar', '=40+2'],
+      ['table', tableExpression],

+        ...body.customRanges!.map((range) => ({
+          ...range,
+          startIndex: range.startIndex + stream.length,
+          endIndex: range.endIndex + stream.length,
+        })),
+      );
+      stream += expression + '\r';
+    }
+  const paragraphIds = new Set<string>();
+  snapshot.body = {
+    ...snapshot.body,

+  };

+  // reaches native mutation validation. Fail at setup with the actual issues.
+  expect(validateDocumentStructure(snapshot)).toEqual([]);
+  new DocumentStore(workspace).save(owner.id, item.id, {
+    snapshot,
+    revision: 0,
+    writeId: crypto.randomUUID(),
+  });
+  const contexts: BrowserContext[] = [];
+  const phone = async (account = false) => {
+    const context = await browser.newContext({
+      baseURL,
+      viewport: { width: 390, height: 844 },
+      deviceScaleFactor: 1,
+      isMobile: true,
+      hasTouch: true,
+      ignoreHTTPSErrors: true,
+      colorScheme: 'light',

+          name: COOKIE_NAME,
+          value: auth.createSession(owner.id).token,
+          url: baseURL.replace('http:', 'https:'),
+          secure: true,
+          httpOnly: true,
+          sameSite: 'Strict',
+        },
+      ]);

+  };
+  const account = await phone(true),
+    page = await account.newPage();
+  const errors: string[] = [];
+  const diagnostics: unknown[] = [];
+  page.on('pageerror', (error) => errors.push(error.message));

+      path: new URL(request.url()).pathname,
+      failure: request.failure()?.errorText,

+  );

+  });
+  page.on('websocket', (socket) => {
+    socket.on('framereceived', ({ payload }) => {
+      try {
+        const frame = JSON.parse(String(payload));
+        if (['ack', 'edit', 'resume', 'resync'].includes(frame.type))
+          diagnostics.push({ received: JSON.stringify(frame).slice(0, 6000) });
+      } catch {
+        // Other sockets may use binary payloads.
+      }
+    });
+    socket.on('framesent', ({ payload }) => {
+      try {
+        const frame = JSON.parse(String(payload));

+  };
+  return {
+    auth,
+    account,
+    page,
+    item,
+    owner,
+    errors,
+    read,
+    phone,
+    async close() {
+      const observed = await Promise.allSettled(
+        contexts
+          .flatMap((context) => context.pages())
+          .map((target) =>
+            target.evaluate(() => ({
+              save: document.querySelector('[role="status"][aria-label="Save status"]')
+                ?.textContent,
+              connection: document.querySelector('[role="status"][aria-label="Connection status"]')

+            })),
+          ),
+      );
+      const persisted = await read().catch((error) => ({ error: String(error) }));
+      await writeFile(
+        info.outputPath('sync-diagnostics.json'),
+        JSON.stringify({ errors, diagnostics, observed, persisted }, null, 2),
+      );

+      db.close();
+    },
+  };
+}

+# SPN-071 — Personal hiding, access provenance and live upgrades
+
+## Scope and capability checkpoint
+
+**2026-11-01 · Accepted implementation direction · agent judgment.** The complete L-sized outcome retains all three scenarios from SPN-071: personal Hide/Show hidden discovery, privacy-safe granting-ancestor details including the Space boundary, and an open viewer becoming editable without reload or lost position. Declining shares, notifications and personal pinning remain out of scope.
+
+Current-main investigation found two unconditional role-mismatch fences: the sync transport closes upgraded sockets and the client treats upgraded metadata as terminal denial. Native permissions already project Spinel grants at the public cache boundary. The implementation will reuse those boundaries, admitting only verified account-role increases on the same native unit. Downgrades, revocation, guest epochs, document generations, maintenance and account changes retain their existing fences. A real Doc and Sheet upgrade is the first capability check; no test pass is claimed in this checkpoint.
+
+Hiding remains a separate per-account discovery preference. It does not change grants, canonical parent, ownership, personal filing or prepared offline bytes. A Space is hidden as its outer file. Access details use current account authorization and expose only readable granting sources; Space children retain the outer Space sharing boundary.
+
+### Persona tradeoffs
+
+- **Collaborator:** fewer stale shares, an explanation of effective access, and live editing without losing their current work or place.
+- **Owner:** ownership, sharing and canonical organization remain authoritative; personal hiding cannot remove a document or alter a grant.
+- **Link guest:** no account discovery or provenance metadata; existing link revocation and privacy epochs remain authoritative.
+- **Operator:** no new service or background polling system; existing bounded collaboration scans and SQLite storage are reused.
+
+## Validation plan
+
+Use focused workspace/HTTP tests for personal isolation, search filtering and nonleaking provenance; native permission and transport tests for upgrade plus downgrade/revocation; production browser journeys for hide/restore and actual Doc/Sheet typing in the unchanged native unit. Cover prepared downloads and the phone document-layout restriction. Add changed production Storybook states and inspect light, dark and phone screenshots.
+
+The final PR must retain the seven required CI gates, two independent nonimplementing reviews of the same current commit, visual approval marked **agent review only**, exact source/check/review identities, measurements, and dispositions. This checkpoint is an implementation plan, not completed acceptance evidence. The original kickoff requested a mergeable PR; the later authorized backlog run resumes it through landing after all gates pass, as recorded below.
+
+## Personal hiding without changing access
+
+**2026-11-01 · Accepted · agent judgment.** The question was whether hiding should
+reuse personal filing, remove a grant or add an independent discovery preference.
+The original ticket and [personal organization decision](SPN-021.md#legacy-decision-30-trash-batches-and-exact-set-deletion)
+require the latter. A private `workspace_hidden` table records only account/item
+pairs. Authorization is checked before each change. Owners, Operators, guests,
+revoked accounts and Space children cannot use that endpoint to create unrelated
+preferences. Cascading foreign keys remove preferences with their account or item.
+
+Ordinary shared/search responses filter hidden rows. The account catalog can
+request the complete authorized inventory, carrying only a `hidden` flag, so
+**Show hidden** and cold offline launch remain useful. Search retains the complete
+graph for scope traversal and filters hidden result rows afterward. This hides
+the selected outer file, not every descendant: hidden folders remain traversable
+where the person has current access. Filed references and downloaded bundles are
+not removed. An outer Space is one preference, without independent child hiding,
+filing or grants. Existing sign-out and revocation cleanup stays authoritative.
+
+The UI composes existing menus, badges, status text and focus restoration. It
+exposes **Hide**, **Show**, and the Shared with me title menu's **Show hidden** /
+**Hide hidden**. Failed requests leave confirmed state visible; pending operations
+use the existing serialized shared-item mutation path. Personal pinning remains
+removed under [decision #128](SPN-047.md#legacy-decision-128-remove-personal-pinning).
+
+**Personas:** the Collaborator controls discovery without losing access or
+downloaded work; the Owner's grants and canonical organization are unchanged;
+the Link guest receives no account catalog; the Operator maintains one small
+SQLite preference table, with restore and sync-transition inventory updated.
+
+## Privacy-safe access provenance
+
+**2026-11-01 · Accepted · agent judgment.** Reusing cached parent labels could
+reveal an ancestor after access changed. Instead, a dedicated account-only access
+endpoint resolves the current effective role and its source in one transaction.
+It chooses the nearest readable grant matching the effective role; direct access
+wins an equal-strength tie. Stronger inherited access still wins over a weaker
+direct grant, following [first integration grooming](grooming-2026-10-17.md#legacy-decision-23-first-integration-grooming).
+Every candidate ancestor must independently be readable before its name is sent.
+Explicit Space scope cannot fall back to ordinary routes, and child grants cannot
+escape the outer Space sharing boundary from
+[decision #116](SPN-078.md#legacy-decision-116-spaces-remain-files-in-folders).
+
+The existing read-only modal presents **Editor through Budgets** or direct/owner
+access, plus the Space boundary when applicable. It fetches only while open,
+rechecks on focus/visibility/online and every five seconds, and clears old names
+on offline/hidden/error states. Request generations reject stale responses. It
+offers no grant editing and never includes other accounts' grants.
+
+**Personas:** the Collaborator learns why they can edit; the Owner retains
+private ancestor names and grant authority; the Link guest receives no account
+provenance; the Operator gets a bounded resolver and current authorization, with
+no new cached permission model. This uses existing modal/menu patterns from the
+[approved composed design](SPN-047.md#legacy-decision-126-approved-redesign-and-its-limits).
+
+## Live upgrades with current authority
+
+**2026-11-01 · Accepted · agent judgment.** The capability checkpoint established
+that public native root permission points can be changed without rebuilding a
+Doc or Sheet. The transport now accepts only monotonic account-role increases
+through its existing access scan; precommit authorization still checks every
+edit. Guests, downgrades, revocations, account changes, route mismatches, maintenance
+and replaced generations keep their existing fences. Old-role one-use tickets
+remain invalid. No new polling mechanism or SDK dependency is introduced.
+
+The existing client access check admits an upgrade only on the same live unit.
+It updates root permissions and native input controls without selecting,
+scrolling, focusing, recreating the unit or reconnecting its socket. Range,
+worksheet and paragraph policies remain in force. The generic image renderer has
+a separate edit flag from the Sheet drawing service. Independent review found
+that setting it true at upgrade could attach late image controls on a protected
+worksheet. Its flag now follows the real composite workbook/active-worksheet
+policy, including point registration, sheet changes and disposal; the SDK retains
+control of existing object transformers. Live phone Docs keep
+their reversible UI containers: Modern layout can enable editing, while
+Traditional layout and changed-layout restrictions remain read-only. Static
+snapshot behavior is unchanged.
+
+A prepared viewer first acquires the existing exclusive writer under offline
+editor admission. The durable update compares account, Space scope, generation,
+base snapshot, revision offset, SDK/schema and maintenance identity, refusing
+pending/recovery/uncertain state or a newer stored checkpoint. Only the role and
+read-only metadata change; native base/image bytes remain intact. The current
+checkpoint is then persisted before native input is enabled. Partial promotion
+is idempotent, failures remain visible and can retry, and a viewer projection
+caused by a lost writer or save failure cannot be thawed as a grant upgrade.
+
+**Personas:** the Collaborator continues at their current place and retains local
+work; the Owner's current authority still decides every durable edit; Link guest
+privacy epochs and guest role changes remain terminal; the Operator reuses the
+existing transport, scan, public permission API, storage lock and recovery fences.
